title: Curvature Diagnostics for Muon and Randomization Tests under Weak Nulls
subtitle: Matrix optimization · Exact inference · Inference compute · Asynchronous post-training
intro: The main reads examine curvature calibration of Muon’s spectral steps and finite-sample validity of Fisher tests for binary outcomes. Briefs cover inference by rewriting, expert replay, recurrence depth and post-training systems. The classic revisits GRPO in DeepSeekMath.
window: November 16–19, 2026 (Philadelphia time, including new announcements and delayed indexing)

blocks.text: At 124M parameters, FineWeb-Edu, 100.7M tokens and three paired seeds, splitting Q/K/V lowers final validation loss by 0.0250 nats versus fused QKV. blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: At 355M, the combination gains 0.0188 nats. Budgets are below one token per parameter, and diagnostics overlapped early screening. The combination saves about 4.3% tokens but takes about 12% more time in the unfused implementation, leaving end-to-end acceleration unestablished. [1]

articles.paper: On the Validity of Fisher Randomization Tests under the Weak Null
articles.authors: Timothy Sudijono · Edgar Dobriban · Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
articles.title: When does a Fisher test remain valid with heterogeneous individual effects?
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 18, 2026 ET · November 19 announcement
articles.evidence: Read Sections 1–2 and Appendix A’s tail comparison and CRE proof

blocks.text: Neyman (1923) targets a sample-average effect. Fisher’s (1935) standard randomization argument assumes zero effect for every unit. This paper fixes binary potential outcomes, uses only assignment randomness, and obtains finite-sample guarantees for three common designs. [2]

blocks.label: Under SUTVA, observe Yᵢ=Yᵢ(Aᵢ). The weak null allows positive and negative effects to cancel.
For the three combinations, the two-sided result holds for all α∈(0,1). The one-sided guarantee for τ≤0 is stated for α≤1/2.

blocks.text: In complete randomization, conditioning on the observed event total O gives reference H∼Hypergeom(n,O,n/2). Counting compatible potential-outcome tables shows that the actual treated-event count is more concentrated, yielding tail control. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The result depends on binary outcomes and the specified statistics. For a general exchangeable design, the paper gives a valid correction by doubling the one-sided p-value. Nonbinary outcomes admit counterexamples. [2]

articles.paper: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
articles.title: Spend forward passes on equivalent rewritings
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 18, 2026 ET · November 19 announcement

blocks.text: For finite-group rewritings such as graph relabeling, the authors approximate an orbit average. The abstract gives worst-case growth with log|G| and compares rewritings with repeated sampling at matched forward-pass counts. The law depends on the required approximation accuracy and does not imply exact recovery with a fixed number of calls. [3]

articles.paper: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
articles.authors: Zhenrui Yue · Gongxiaohui Chen · Huimin Zeng · Honglei Zhuang · Jiashuo Sun · Zhen Han · Dong Wang
articles.title: Reuse the chronological order of expert training logs
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 18, 2026 ET · November 19 announcement

blocks.text: MRPD replays trajectories containing behavior probabilities and rewards in each expert’s training order, recomputes policy gradients and distills final experts at logged prefixes. The abstract reports better consolidation than online distillation on three long-horizon domains, without new environment calls. Log order matters more than amount or rewards. [4]

blocks.text: TabPFNv2-style experiments find optimistic configuration selection when too few evaluation datasets are used. Expanding model size and compute also requires expanding maximum synthetic-task rows and features for more reliable extrapolation. [5]

articles.paper: Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models
articles.title: Component interactions need replicated comparisons
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 18, 2026 ET · November 19 announcement

blocks.text: In a two-seed fractional factorial at shared model setting, data and budget, MoE, Muon and a Gated DeltaNet hybrid give larger average improvements. Some second- and third-order effects are aliased, and MoE has more total parameters. The design does not identify every higher-order interaction. [6]

articles.paper: A Differential Theory of Quality-Resource Trade-offs for AI Model Selection: The Multiresource Frontier and Its Minimax Price
articles.title: Extracting multi-resource trade-offs from fitted frontiers
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 15, 2026 ET · November 19 announcement

blocks.text: The author develops a differential representation of error frontiers over latency, parameters, training compute and energy, deriving minimax prices under a channel model. The abstract reports evaluation on 117 published frontiers. The price conclusions depend on the assumed frontier and resource model. [7]

articles.paper: ICICLE: In-Context Inference for Curve-Learning Extrapolation
articles.authors: Laurits Fredsgaard · Michael Riis Andersen · Mikkel N. Schmidt
articles.title: A learning-curve surrogate accepts variable hyperparameter sets
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 18, 2026 ET · November 19 announcement

blocks.text: A 1.28M-parameter surrogate trained on synthetic priors supports freeze–thaw allocation using a shared set encoder for variable hyperparameter counts. Mean-regret trajectories resemble FT-PFN on LCBench, PD1 and TaskSet. Some Meta-Album subsets improve over Quick-Tune, while others show no clear difference. [8]

articles.paper: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
articles.authors: Ziqi Jin · Jiaxi Li · Weiwen Xu · Aixin Sun
articles.title: New tokens skip early loops while retaining deep context
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 18, 2026 ET · November 19 announcement

blocks.text: Late entry runs new tokens through only the final K loops while completing old-token caches to depth T. Wake verifies candidates using completed states. Exact and lossy modes are reported separately. Ouro’s 5.2× exact-mode speedup is against the tokenwise baseline, versus +26% over full K=T block decoding. [9]

articles.paper: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
articles.title: DaisyRose’s long-horizon tasks and asynchronous pipeline
articles.evidence: Read task construction, backend and evaluation notes

blocks.text: About 1,200 selected tasks were trained over 18 days on 144 H200s, with 128 for rollouts and 16 for the trainer. Sessions up to 1M tokens are split into trajectories through harness summaries, while native context stays at 256K. Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 rises from 5.6 to 12.0. Reported benchmark scores select the higher BF16/FP8 result per benchmark. [10]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The team reports backend MFU of 37% versus 16% and end-to-end throughput of 16,800 versus 8,300 tokens/s. Multipliers depend on the compared backends and task settings, with independent-system replication still outstanding. [10]

articles.paper: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say
articles.authors: Bruno Duarte · Gabriel Pimenta de Freitas Cardoso · Isis F. Carvalho · Breno de Almeida Beleza · Felipe Lima
articles.title: SFT duration needs evaluation and checkpoint overheads
articles.evidence: Read data, predictors, results and limitations

blocks.text: Across 272 H200 jobs covering LoRA and full SFT, the target is elapsed time from GPU allocation to completion, excluding queueing. CatBoost uses pre-dispatch configuration, cumulative evaluation volume and checkpoint volume. Stratified five-fold MAE is 1.71 hours versus 12.41 for the best tested FLOP baseline. Mean job duration is 23.43 hours. [11]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The data come from one production environment. Feature importance describes predictive associations, and transfer across hardware remains unverified. [11]

articles.paper: A 9B model beats a 1T model on FinQA, trained with Crusoe Managed RL
articles.authors: Matan Halfon · Itay Niv · Daniel Shen · Suman Debnath · Yiwei Song · Omri Berkovitch
articles.title: Dynamic sampling and prompt revisiting on FinQA
articles.evidence: Read task and evaluation protocol and Tables 3–4

blocks.text: GRPO uses 16 rollouts per prompt. Half the prompts are fresh and half revisit unmastered prompts weighted by p(1−p), while equal-reward groups are filtered. Qwen3.5-9B rises from 53.1% to 73.9% on 290 external SnorkelFinance questions. Trained scores use each run’s peak checkpoint. [12]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The 35B-A3B ablations are single runs. The reported held-out run-to-run variation is about ±7 percentage points, leaving most ablation differences within that noise range. [12]

classic.question: At fixed rollout-token budget, which distributions of per-question success probabilities change the optimal trade-off between group size G and the number of distinct questions?

blocks.text: PPO (2017) typically uses a separate value network. DeepSeekMath (2024) samples a group of answers per question and constructs advantages from relative group rewards. Here we focus on outcome supervision, with fixed sampling policy πold and response length Tᵢ. [13]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The rows compare the paper’s SFT and RL stages, without a matched-budget causal decomposition of PPO versus GRPO. Group normalization, sequence averaging and clipping change estimator weights, so the complete objective does not directly equal unbiased vanilla REINFORCE. [13]
